transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-08-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: 00:55
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Carlos Reyes (Medwise Head of ML), Maya Patel (Product), Samir Khan (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): discuss POC quality eval plan, success criteria (accuracy, hallucination rate, format fidelity), workload sizing for benchmarks, timelines. Action items recorded.

Topics:
- Success criteria and pass/fail thresholds
- Workload sizing and benchmark types (p95 latency, tokens/sec, cold vs warm KV cache)
- Golden prompt set and regression tests
- Hallucination and format checks + scoring approach
- Security and data residency constraints

Transcript: 
[00:00] Jordan: Okay, great, good afternoon everyone, um this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Priya: Hi team, hi, yeah thanks for making time, we wanted to make sure we align on exactly how you're going to evaluate quality in the POC and what we need to run the benchmarks.
[00:17] Carlos: Thanks, Jordan, Priya. Quick context: at Medwise we have two main flows we care about — clinical note summarization for provider inbox, and a question-answering flow for patient FAQs. Our priority is zero-tolerance hallucinations for the clinical flow, and consistent formatting for billing codes.
[00:32] Maya: Also timeline: our leadership wants a decision within three weeks of the POC start, so we need tight benchmarks and clear pass/fail.
[00:40] Priya: Understood. For the quality eval plan we usually split into golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, format/serialization checks, and an overall scoring rubric. We'll propose thresholds for each.
[00:51] Jordan: Quick check — are you planning to run this on Redwood Hosted or Dedicated or Private? That will affect latency expectations and the exact benchmark setup.
[00:58] Carlos: We want to try Hosted first for speed, but if the dedicated SLAs look better we may consider Dedicated or Private later — security may push us to Private for production. For the POC hosted is fine.
[01:10] Samir: From security perspective, POC on Hosted is acceptable as long as the data is de-identified and we have agreement on retention. We'll need SOC2 docs and KMS integration details before moving to Dedicated.
[01:20] Priya: Noted. For the eval plan: golden prompts — we ask customers to provide a set of canonical examples (we usually ask for 30-100 depending on complexity). These are the "source of truth" for correctness. Regression set should be larger — 200 to 1,000 examples to exercise edge cases.
[01:36] Carlos: We can do 50 golden prompts and about 300 regression examples. We'll include edge cases around incomplete notes and ambiguous codes.
[01:44] Priya: Perfect. Scoring approach: we do per-example checks with multiple criteria: exact-match for structured outputs (e.g., ICD-10 codes), semantic similarity for free-text summaries (embedding-based), and hallucination flags. We'll output a composite score (weighted).
[01:56] Jordan: Can you expand on hallucination checks? How do you normally detect or score hallucination?
[02:02] Priya: Sure. Two levels: automated heuristics and manual spot checks. Automated heuristics include contradiction detection, provenance absence for factual claims, and entity hallucination detection — e.g., a model inventing a medication that isn't in the record. We also include hallucination density (hallucinations per 1k tokens) and a pass/fail if over X%. Manual checks sample 5-10% of outputs focusing on high-risk cases.
[02:22] Carlos: For clinical flow we want zero hallucination tolerance on medication attribution — that's basically an immediate fail if detected. Is that realistic?
[02:29] Priya: Zero is tough but we can set a very low threshold for automated detection and flag any occurrence as critical. For POC we can surface the false positives from heuristics as part of the report so you can see the signal vs noise.
[02:40] Maya: For formatting — billing codes have to be exact format, no extra punctuation. We need to be able to run regex checks and produce a pass/fail per example.
[02:48] Priya: Absolutely. For structured outputs like codes we use strict exact-match and a separate normalized-match where we remove punctuation/casing. We log both.
[02:56] Jordan: Workload sizing for benchmarks — Carlos, can you share expected QPS and average lengths?
[03:02] Carlos: For production: peak burst ~50 qps, sustained ~10 qps. Average request size for summarization is about 2,500 tokens (clinical notes are long), and for FAQ it's shorter, ~150 tokens. We'll start POC with 1k example runs to simulate load.
[03:16] Priya: Good, for the runtime benchmarks we'll run three scenarios: single-request p95 latency at typical batch sizes, throughput test (tokens/sec) with continuous stream, and cold vs warm cache runs to show KV cache impact. Note: sometimes transcription says KV cash or KV cache misread.
[03:29] Carlos: Sorry what's the KV cache impact?
[03:31] Priya: KV cache stores key/value attention state for long context to speed up subsequent tokens. Warm runs where KV cache is primed show much lower latency for long sequences. We'll report cold first-request latencies and warm steady-state.
[03:42] Jordan: For the POC we'll plan to run: (1) accuracy/quality eval on the golden/regression sets, (2) throughput & latency benchmarks under the two workload profiles, (3) hallucination analysis report, and (4) a short human review sample.
[03:55] Maya: How do you compute the composite score?
[03:58] Priya: We recommend weights: 40% clinical accuracy (entity-level checks and hallucination), 30% formatting/structured exact-match, 20% semantic similarity for summaries, 10% latency/operational. We can of course adjust weights per your priorities.
[04:13] Carlos: That sounds reasonable. We want an explicit pass threshold for the POC — what do you recommend?
[04:17] Priya: For a first-pass POC: composite >= 85% with zero critical hallucinations for clinical medication attribution, and p95 latency under 1.2s for the FAQ flow, and p95 under 3.5s for the long summarization when warm. Those numbers are tunable.
[04:31] Jordan: We'll also provide a written eval template (CSV/JSONL) with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output, check_type, scoring_fn, notes. That will make it reproducible.
[04:41] Carlos: Good. On infrastructure, for hosted POC, what do we need to provide?
[04:46] Priya: For Hosted we just need the prompt sets and de-identified payloads, plus an allow-listed test IP if you want to lock access. For Dedicated/Private we will discuss provisioning windows.
[04:55] Samir: For the security docs, we need SOC2 type II report, KMS integration details (do you support BYOK/HSM?), and a table of retention defaults. Also in the POC we want logs and auditability — can we get request-level logs?
[05:07] Jordan: Yes we can share SOC2 artifacts; Redwood supports KMS and BYOK on Dedicated and Private — on Hosted we have managed keys but can discuss encryption in transit and at rest. We'll upload the security pack to your S3 link.
[05:19] Priya: Regarding eval harness: we'll provide a Python runner that accepts JSONL golden/regression files, runs the model via the API, and computes the scoring functions (exact match, normalized match, embedding-sim, hallucination heuristics). It will output a CSV summary and per-example logs for manual triage.
[05:33] Maya: For embedding-based similarity, what threshold do you use?
[05:36] Priya: We usually recommend 0.85 cosine for high precision on short summaries, but we calibrate on your golden set and can show ROC curves so you can pick a threshold.
[05:45] Carlos: For hallucination heuristics — can you show sample rules?
[05:48] Priya: Examples: medication not present in input, contradictory assertion, invented entity with low provenance score. We'll flag and put a confidence score on the heuristic. As Jordan said we'll include manual sampling to validate false positives.
[05:58] Jordan: Timelines: if you provide the golden/regression sets by Friday (2025-08-08), Priya can deliver the harness by 2025-08-12, we run benchmarks 2025-08-13 to 2025-08-14, and we review results on 2025-08-18. That fits your 3-week decision window.
[06:14] Carlos: That's tight but doable, we'll aim to hit the Friday cutoff.
[06:18] Samir: For data residency — production may need EU region. For POC hosted can it run in us-east?
[06:24] Jordan: POC in US regions is fine; production can be pinned to EU or dedicated private infra if needed.
[06:30] Maya: A couple practical Qs: will you run the eval with the exact versions of the model? How do you handle model updates?
[06:37] Priya: We'll pin the model version and record the model hash. For POC we use a stable snapshot. If you want we can include tests for rollback behavior or regression across two model versions.
[06:48] Jordan: Also, about cost — we'll share an estimate for tokens consumed in the POC and two replacement options: hosted pay-as-you-go and a committed Dedicated bundle.
[06:56] Carlos: Please include cost per 1M tokens and an example cost projection for 100k summary runs.
[07:02] Priya: We'll add that. One more logistic: for human review, how many reviewers do you want? Sampling 5-10% of outputs with two reviewers to compute inter-rater agreement is common.
[07:13] Carlos: We'll start with a single clinical reviewer due to bandwidth, but we can escalate if needed.
[07:18] Priya: Ok. Any red flags or blockers from your side?
[07:22] Samir: Nothing major, just need the security pack and explicit retention periods. And we'll want an NDA addendum for PHI handling if we move from de-identified to limited PHI.
[07:33] Jordan: We'll coordinate legal and get the NDA addendum template started.
[07:37] Maya: Recap please?
[07:39] Jordan: Sure. Recap: 1) Carlos to deliver 50 golden prompts + 300 regression examples by 2025-08-08; 2) Jordan to send pricing + Dedicated options by 2025-08-07; 3) Priya to deliver eval harness + scoring script by 2025-08-12; 4) Redwood runs benchmarks 2025-08-13/14; 5) Follow-up review 2025-08-18. Also security docs from Redwood and SOC2/KMS details from Samir.
[07:57] Maya: Sounds good.
[07:59] Carlos: Thanks team.
[08:01] Jordan: Thanks everyone — we'll send calendar invite for the 8/18 review and upload the eval template.
[08:08] Priya: Bye all.

(Transcript ends — automated timestamps approximate; transcription may contain misheard proper nouns such as "KV cash" or "Redwood privet" in places.)
